armored-mount: - Apply half your Maneuvering in Armor skill to your mount (and your full skill to yourself as usual).
aspect-of-fear:
- +10 to any Intimidation maneuver during battle.
- Any enemy within 30' making an RR against fear (any source): -10 to that RR. Not cumulative if several combatants have this ability.
assess-the-field:
- With a successful Perception maneuver, determine the approximate condition of **all visible** allies and enemies: penalties for hits lost (-10 for 26-50% of hits lost, -20 for 51-75%, -30 for 76% or more), stun, fatigue, injuries.
- Without the ability: the same assessment for a single individual only, or a more general overview of the field.
battle-line:
- Spend one round calling directions (Concentration) to a contiguous group of allies (each within melee range of the closest ally on each side): they get a bonus of **2x your Leadership ranks** to Protect maneuvers.
- Lasts until an ally is no longer adjacent to any ally from the original group, or the battle ends.
binding-chain: - You may bind/entangle: attack at -10, but any critical inflicted is a **Grapple** critical.
brave-legion: - +20 to RRs against fear if an ally is within 5'; +30 if you have an ally on each side.
bullrush:
- On a shield bash, you may knock the foe back **instead of dealing a critical**: use Table 4.2a by the critical severity achieved. The foe must make a medium Running or Acrobatics maneuver (their choice) to remain standing.
- Decide before rolling the critical.

#### Table 4.2a - Bullrush Critical Effects

| Critical Severity | Effect |
|---|---|
| A | +5 Hits, Knocked back 5' |
| B | +10 Hits, Stagger, KB 5' |
| C | +15 Hits, Stagger, KB 10' |
| D | +20 Hits, Stun[-25], KB 10' |
| E | +25 Hits, Stun[-50], KB 15' |
careful-shot: - After rolling the attack but before rolling the critical (if any), you may decide not to take the shot: the arrow/bolt is saved and, if concealed, your location is not revealed.
concealed-strike:
- While drawing a concealed weapon (normal 1 AP draw, unless Quickdraw talent), make a Trickery maneuver as a free action, opposed by the foe's Perception.
- If Trickery wins: the foe applies **no DB from Quickness, Parry or Dodge** against your next attack with that weapon in the same or following round.
- A foe who has seen you use it gets +30 to Perception against it.
- Not sufficient to allow Ambush skill (see Improved Concealed Strike).
coordinated-maneuver: - When two or more allies are within melee range of a single foe: after one round of directions (Concentration), each such ally gets a bonus to OB **or** DB equal to your Leadership ranks, for all attacks in the same or subsequent round.
defensive-bash: - When shield bashing, you keep half the shield's base DB (e.g. +10 for a normal shield), but still no passive block. Without it, a shield used to attack gives no DB.
defensive-ward:
- Defend with the off-hand weapon instead of attacking with it (no attack with it that round).
- It acts as a shield with base **+5 DB vs melee only** (not ranged), using Multiple Attacks skill in place of Shield skill: passive block (add Multiple Attacks ranks to DB) or partial/full block (based on Multiple Attacks skill bonus).
- Passive block and passive dodge are not cumulative.
- A dagger blocks one attack; any other weapon may block two.
dirty-fighting: - +10 to any maneuver to use a combat trick (see Combat Tricks, Chapter 1).
double-shot:
- Load and fire two arrows at once. Loading two arrows takes +2 AP (+1 AP with Improved Quickload).
- Both attacks against the same target or adjacent targets, at no more than Short range, each at -10.
dual-draw: - Draw and ready two one-handed weapons as a single action: 1 AP, or instantaneous with the Quickdraw talent.
evade-shield: - The foe's total shield DB (including Shield skill or rank bonus from blocking) is **halved** against your attacks with a suitable weapon.
experienced-rider: - +10 to Mounted Combat and +5 to Riding.
expert-defense: - While actively calling guidance to an ally (Concentration): for every -2 OB they apply to parry, they get **+3 DB** (instead of +2).
fast-crank: - Load and cock a light or hand crossbow in 3 AP (normally 6), a heavy crossbow in 10 AP (normally 14).
feint:
- Spend 1 AP for a Feint: conflicted maneuver, your weapon skill vs the foe's weapon skill.
- On success, the foe's active DB (quickness, parry, dodge, shield; not armor bonus or protection effective in all directions) is **halved** for your next attack action in the same or following round.
fight-free: - If a foe has less than a 100% grapple on you, any grapple penalty to your unarmed attacks is halved.
focused-strike:
- You must be able to make multiple attacks with no penalty. For each such attack you give up: **+15 OB** to your remaining attack.
- If giving up attacks with a shield or secondary weapon, you get no benefit from those items (e.g. no defensive shield benefit).
from-the-shoulder:
- Apply the armor **Perception** penalty to crossbow shots in place of the armor Ranged attack penalty.
- Cover penalty for shooting past allies is halved.
get-inside:
- Your attacks must have a much smaller melee range than the opponent's:
  - Same Size: they must use at least a one-handed weapon that is not light (not a -1 Size adjustment weapon), and you may use only unarmed attacks or a dagger.
  - If they wield a two-handed weapon or are larger Size than you: you may also use a light weapon.
  - Cannot be used against a smaller-Size foe.
- After an attack that scores a critical, you may advance into the foe's space. Any in-progress attack by that foe against you (AP already spent) is at **-10 for a weapon 2' or longer, -20 for 4' or longer**, even if they move away before resolving it. The foe may use Restricted Quarters skill to cancel these penalties.
- While in their space, you move and act on their initiative (staying with them as they move).
- Faster Rounds optional rule (Core Law 8.2): the penalty applies to the foe's next attack if it occurs in the current or next round.
grab-and-slam:
- After an attack that results in a grapple, as a free action slam the foe into a surface: resolve as a **Ram attack with OB = total grapple percentage**.
- Max once per round. With multiple grapple-capable attacks, you may wait until the last one resolves (if the foe is still grappled).
greater-adrenal-defense: - Adrenal Defense lasts one additional round per full 5 the maneuver succeeded by (instead of the normal round per full 20, doubled).
greater-adrenal-speed: - Adrenal Speed lasts one additional round per full 10 the maneuver succeeded by (instead of per full 20).
greater-adrenal-strength: - Adrenal Strength lasts one additional round per full 10 the maneuver succeeded by (instead of per full 20).
heedless-fury: - Anyone attacking you in melee gets +20 OB, but your attack is treated as **one size larger**.
hook-shield:
- Make a Disarm maneuver with your weapon OB (Core Law 9.7) but with no weapon-type modifiers.
- On success, instead of disarming: the foe's total shield DB (including Shield skill bonus) is **halved** until you attack with the axe/hook weapon, or they move away and you do not follow; minimum one round.
- On absolute success: shield DB completely nullified for the same duration.
improved-concealed-strike: - When using Concealed Strike, add up to half your Ambush ranks (if any) to the critical result.
improved-frenzy: - +10 to Adrenal Focus maneuvers to begin or end a Frenzy.
improved-parry: - When parrying in this style, each -2 OB gives **+3 DB** (not +2).
improved-quickdraw: - First weapon draw in a round is Instantaneous (0 AP) as per Quickdraw; additional draws are free actions (no AP). Useful for throwing several weapons per round.
improved-quickload: - First loading action in a round is Instantaneous (0 AP) as per Quickload; additional loading actions in the same round are free actions (no AP).
improvised-weapons:
- Any unsuitability penalty of an improvised weapon is reduced by 20 (e.g. firewood as a -30 club becomes -10).
- Does not reduce similarity penalties (without the club melee specialization, the usual similarity penalty still applies).
jumping-the-order: - A focused, timed order (Concentration) shifts an ally's initiative for the round to immediately follow your own.
keep-at-bay:
- When an opponent with a smaller combat range (shorter reach) tries to close to melee with you, you may resolve any in-progress attack before their attack is resolved.
- Your attack gets the normal modification for AP spent if fewer than 4; you may use your next AP of the round (if any remain) to complete the attack.
- If your attack scores a critical, the foe must succeed at a Running or Acrobatics maneuver; on failure, they cannot enter melee range and cannot strike you. The maneuver is at **-10 per critical severity above A** (e.g. -30 for D) and **+20 per size the foe is larger** than you.
- Faster Rounds optional rule (Core Law 8.2): the defender can keep the foe at bay as long as they have not attacked before the foe tries to move into range.
killing-strike: - Take -10 to OB and DB for the round to get **+5 on all critical rolls** for the round.
lancers-knockback:
- On a mounted charge against a target on foot, you may choose (before rolling the critical) to knock the foe back.
- If a critical is achieved: severity reduced by one, foe knocked back 5' per critical severity, and must make a medium Running or Acrobatics maneuver to remain standing.
leg-sweep: - Decide before the attack to try to trip. If you score a critical, its severity is reduced by one and the foe must **exceed your total attack roll** with a Running maneuver to avoid being knocked prone.
lend-expertise:
- Coach an ally who accepts your instructions to grant them one **combat talent** you have (not a fighting style ability). The ally must be equipped appropriately and meet the prerequisites (style, ability, talents).
- Requires Concentration for one round. The ally may use the talent once (or for one round if it has a duration), in the same round or within **one round per two Leadership ranks** you have.
- An ally may benefit from only one granted talent at a time.
lightning-reflexes:
- Start the round wielding suitable weapons (or unarmed): **+5 initiative**. With Quickdraw, also if your hands are free and empty and you will draw suitable weapons.
- Selectable multiple times; cumulative.
loyal-protector: - +10 to Protect skill when using this ability.
marshals-voice: - +10 to Leadership skill when using this style.
mountain-stance:
- Count as one size larger (or 4x your weight) against any feat of strength trying to move you.
- Any knockback/forced movement (e.g. critical knockback) is halved.
- You may make a Physical RR to resist being knocked prone.
mounts-attack:
- Direct your mount to attack: resolved in the same phase as your attack, with the mount's OB, as if the mount spent the same AP as you did on your attack.
- Your Mounted Combat skill may offset any pace penalty on this attack.
move-together:
- Any number of allies with this ability plus one designated leader (with Leadership skill), all in a single group (no gaps over 5'), may move and act on the **leader's initiative**. Choose before initiative is determined for the round.
- The leader's initiative bonus is modified by **-5, +1 per 3 full Leadership ranks**.
off-hand-dagger: - No off-hand penalty (normally -20 without the Ambidextrous talent) for a dagger in the off-hand. Multiple-attack penalties still apply.
off-hand-light-weapon: - No off-hand penalty for any light weapon (-1 Size adjustment: e.g. short sword, epee, machete, light flail, hand axe, light mace) in the off-hand. Multiple-attack penalties still apply.
overbearing: - On a shield bash, you may inflict **Unbalancing** criticals instead of Krush. Decide before rolling the critical.
pain-resistance: - On any Fortitude maneuver, all fatigue, injury and Stun penalties to it are halved.
paired-weapon-attack:
- Make a single attack roll with the primary weapon (no multiple-weapon penalties), treated as **one size larger**.
- No other benefit from the secondary weapon that round (no defensive ward, no extra attack).
pommel-strike:
- Make two attacks with the weapon, treated as two attacks with two different weapons, with the usual Katas modifiers, mitigated by Multiple Attacks skill (Core Law 9.7). Generally -75 to each attack against the same foe or -95 against two different foes, reduced by Multiple Attacks skill.
- The attacks use different parts of the weapon, with the same melee specialization OB. The second attack is **one size smaller**, on a table for the second striking surface: quarterstaff or pole arm haft -> fighting stick table; two-handed sword pommel -> mace table.
precise-target:
- Called-shot penalty to a location reduced to **-10** (normally -25).
- Applies to one Ranged Weapon specialization (e.g. Bow, Crossbow, Thrown) designated by the style.
protect-mount: - +25 when using Protect skill to protect your mount (parry or shield).
protected-rider: - Once per round when targeted, make a Medium (+0) Riding maneuver to use the mount to protect yourself: the attack is resolved against the mount with all normal modifiers.
push-through-it: - Successful Leadership maneuver (Concentration): reduce an ally's accumulated stun by 2 rounds; partial success 1 round; absolute success 3 rounds.
quick-to-action:
- Successful Leadership maneuver (Concentration), made after battle has begun: allies within 30' get **+2 initiative** for the rest of the battle.
- Can be repeated to extend the bonus to allies outside the original 30', but not to increase it.
raging-wind: - Starting the round in a Frenzy: +5 initiative.
redirect: - Before rolling a critical, you may reduce its severity by one: the foe is moved **5' per critical severity (before reduction)** in a direction you choose, but not more than the distance they moved last round.
ride-as-one: - You and your mount move and act on the same initiative, using whichever has the higher initiative bonus.
ride-under-cover: - Use the mount as cover against all attacks from the front and one side: **half hard cover (+40 vs melee, +80 vs ranged)**. Maintaining the posture requires Concentration.
second-rank: - No penalty for attacking past an ally with a pole arm (normally -40, -20 for pole arms).
seen-it: - When a foe uses a combat trick (Chapter 1) against you, the trick's difficulty is increased by **two degrees** (e.g. Medium -> Very Hard).
shadowblade:
- +10 to Blindfighting skill while using the granting style.
- If your modified Blindfighting exceeds what is needed to cancel your darkness penalty, and the foe is subject to a darkness penalty, add up to +10 of the excess to your DB against that foe.
sharp-words: - +10 to any Influence maneuver during combat.
shield-bash:
- While attacking, you may shield bash as an **additional attack** instead of using the shield defensively (no DB from shield or blocking that round).
- No penalty if both attacks target the same foe; -20 to both attacks if weapon and shield target two different foes.
- Cannot be combined with any other additional attacks (a limited version of Katas, Core Law 9.7, and Multiple Attacks skill).
- Alternative: +25 to Multiple Attacks skill as long as one of your attacks is a shield bash.
shield-press:
- After a successful shield bash (scored a critical), you may advance into the foe's space with the shield pressed against them (or their shield).
- Any in-progress attack by that foe against you is at **-10 for a weapon 2' or longer, -20 for 4' or longer**, even if they move away before resolving it; foe's Restricted Quarters skill can cancel these penalties.
- Faster Rounds optional rule (Core Law 8.2): applies to the foe's next attack if it occurs in the current or next round.
shield-wall: - When fighting within 5' of at least one ally with a shield and using the Protect maneuver, both you and the protected ally get the **full** parry DB (normally it is divided between you).
shieldbreaker:
- When trying to break a shield: +20 on the maneuver to break it, and if successful the shield gets -25 on its breakage check.
- Procedure (summary of Treasure Law rules): instead of an attack, make an **absolute maneuver with your weapon skill**, modified per Table 4.2b; on success, the shield makes a breakage check with the breakage roll modifiers below.
- Optimal weapons: an axe for a wooden shield, a mace to crush a metal one.

#### Table 4.2b - Shield Breaking Modifiers

| Situation | Mod. |
|---|---|
| **Attack/maneuver bonuses** | |
| Attacker | +weapon OB |
| Optimal weapon | +10 |
| Two-handed weapon | +10 |
| Each size larger | +10 |
| Shieldbreaker ability | +20 |
| **Defense penalties to maneuver** | |
| Defender | -shield skill ranks |
| Shield | -base shield DB |
| Shield material is stronger than weapon | -difference |
| **Breakage roll modifiers** | |
| Absolute Failure | Roll breakage for weapon |
| Partial success | +20 |
| Success | +0 |
| Absolute success | -25 |
| Optimal weapon | -10 |
| Two-handed weapon | -10 |
| Each size larger | -10 |
| Shield material is stronger than weapon | +difference |
| Shieldbreaker ability | -25 |
shoot-from-cover:
- Firing from behind cover: no penalty for obstructions within 10' of your position (if there is enough opening to attack).
- Perception to find your exact location: -20 (partial cover), -40 (half cover), -100 (full cover, 90% or more).
shot-on-the-run: - Use half your Footwork skill bonus when moving while making a bow or crossbow attack (normally Footwork only applies to melee and thrown attacks).
slowing-shot:
- On an attack against the target's legs that deals a critical (called shot or by chance), you may choose before rolling to slow the target: critical severity reduced by one; the target's BMR is reduced by **5' per original critical severity**, to a minimum of half their original BMR.
- If the critical inflicts an injury penalty, BMR stays impaired until the injury heals; otherwise it recovers after ten minutes of rest.
split-focus: - +25 to any maneuver to keep a foe from your flank or rear arc (if you are aware of them). See Facing and Flanking, Core Law 9.5.
steady-shield: - The number of attacks you may use your shield against is increased by one. Selectable multiple times; cumulative.
sweeping-parry: - Instead of splitting the parry between opponents, reduce the parry amount by 10 per additional foe and apply the rest against every attack of each foe in the round.
swift-footed: - BMR +5' while in combat (and using the style), for movement up to Run (3x) pace. Selectable multiple times; cumulative.
throw-and-melee:
- In a multiple attack action (Katas with Multiple Attacks skill), one or more attacks may be thrown weapon attacks.
- The thrown attack may be resolved in an earlier phase, with the usual penalties if fewer than 3 AP were spent.
trample:
- The mount makes a Trample attack against every foe in a straight-line path; each foe must be at least **two sizes smaller** than the mount (Large warhorse -> Medium targets; Big horse or pony -> Small targets).
- 4 AP action for the rider; OB = mount's kicking or trampling attack + your Riding ranks.
trick-shot: - Cover modifiers to your attacks are halved, if you know the target's position.
two-handed-grip: - Grip a one-handed weapon with both hands: normal +10 OB two-handed modifier, and **x1.5 concussion hits**.
unarmed-parry: - Unarmed and unarmored combatants normally have restricted parry (half parry DB vs weapon attacks). With this ability you get the full parry even unarmed against an armed opponent.
vigilant: - +10 to Perception, only to detect threats (ambush, hidden weapons, traps). Applies in and out of combat, as long as you are not using any ability of another fighting style at the same time.
walk-it-off: - One round inspiring allies (Concentration): bonus of **2x your Leadership ranks** to their Fortitude maneuvers, until they fail a Fortitude maneuver or the battle ends.
weapon-breaker: - Decide before attacking to try to break the foe's weapon. If you score a critical: severity reduced by one (e.g. D -> C) and their weapon makes a breakage check at -25.
weapon-form-dagger:
- Make weapon attacks using an appropriate Unarmed Combat specialization defined by the style, with the modifier below. A specific weapon must be selected (e.g. broadsword, light flail).

#### Table 4.2c - Weapon Form Modifiers and Costs

| Weapon | Specialization | Cost. |
|---|---|---|
| Dagger | Strikes -10 | 2 |
| Small net | Wrestling -10 | 2 |
| Light weapon | Strikes -20 | 3 |
| Light flail | Strikes/Sweeps -20 | 3 |
| Net | Wrestling -20 | 3 |
| 1H Weapon | Strikes -20 | 5 |
| 1H Chain/flail | Strikes/Sweeps -20 | 5 |
| Quarterstaff | Strikes/Sweeps -20 | 4 |

\* A light weapon is a weapon with a -1 Size adjustment, such as the hand axe, short sword, machete, light flail, light mace, or light stick.

- Wyvern Style's "Weapon Form: Dagger or Short Sword (3)" matches the Light weapon cost (short sword is a light weapon).
weapon-form-dagger-or-short-sword:
- Make weapon attacks using an appropriate Unarmed Combat specialization defined by the style, with the modifier below. A specific weapon must be selected (e.g. broadsword, light flail).

- Make weapon attacks using an appropriate Unarmed Combat specialization defined by the style, with the modifier below. A specific weapon must be selected (e.g. broadsword, light flail).

zone-of-control:
- When a foe leaves your melee range (including passing through) without a cautious retreat (moving backwards at half speed up to Jog pace; Withdrawing, Core Law 8.2), you may make an immediate melee attack with a readied weapon as an instantaneous action. It does not interrupt any action in progress (e.g. an in-progress attack on another foe) and costs no AP beyond the instantaneous action requirement.
- Resolved as a **2 AP attack (-50)**; selected twice: **3 AP (-25)**; selected three times: **4 AP (no penalty)**.
